items.title: Live: Government will adjust Iran visitor visa rules as war develops, Burke says
items.description: Some Iranian visitor visa holders will be temporarily restricted from entering Australia, the federal government says. Meanwhile, several countries across the Middle East confirm Iran has sent drone and missile strikes across the region. Follow live.

items.title: Trump administration offers 15-point ceasefire plan to Iran
items.description: The ceasefire plan comes as the US military prepares to call up at least 1,000 more troops to supplement those already in the Middle East.

items.title: Australian shares soar on Middle East ceasefire hopes
items.description: The local share market has its best day in almost a year after reports the US is seeking a ceasefire with Iran buoyed investor sentiment, and monthly inflation was softer than expected.

items.title: Government says 5 per cent inflation scenario 'pretty conservative now'
items.description: The government has requested new Treasury modelling for "more challenging circumstances" stemming from the Middle East war, admitting that the economic scenarios released last week "look pretty conservative now".

items.title: Seconds before LaGuardia crash, controller cleared fire truck to cross runway
items.description: US investigators are working to determine which of the airport's safety precautions failed and allowed the fire truck onto the runway, resulting in a collision that killed two pilots.

items.title: Democrats flip seat in Florida district home to Mar-a-Lago resort
items.description: Democrats celebrate the victory as the latest sign voters are turning against Donald Trump and Republicans ahead of November's midterm elections.

items.title: 'Something really shifted': Inside the software company that laid off 40pc of its staff
items.description: As big tech companies sack staff and say AI will pick up the slack, workers are left to grapple with what's really going on.

items.title: Australia warns Israel against south Lebanon occupation
items.description: Australia warns Israel against occupying parts of Lebanon, urging it to respect international law after the displacement of more than 1 million people.

items.title: ABC managing director apologises to audience, amid strike action
items.description: A majority of staff who voted rejected the broadcaster's latest pay offer on the three-year enterprise bargaining agreement, which paved the way for the strike action.

items.title: NASA pivots to moon base, nuclear propulsion in expanded multi-billion-dollar program
items.description: NASA has cancelled plans to deploy a space station in lunar orbit and will instead build a $28.7 billion base on the moon's surface.

items.title: Meta ordered to pay $538m in US trial over child exploitation claims
items.description: The verdict marks the first time a jury has ruled on such claims against Meta, as the company faces a wave of lawsuits over how its platforms affect young people's mental health.

items.title: Could Cyclone Narelle come as far south as Perth?
items.description: Tropical Cyclone Narelle is now barrelling towards Western Australia. Could this unusual cyclone make it all the way to Perth, and how does climate change affect it?

items.title: 'Major player' charged over Sydney grandfather's alleged kidnapping murder
items.description: Police allege the 23-year-old man was a "major player" in organising the abduction plot.

items.title: Ships are escaping the Strait of Hormuz and one is headed for Australia
items.description: The Japanese-owned Iron Maiden will be the first known ship to dock in Australia after it was stranded in the Persian Gulf when the US and Israel began bombing Iran on February 28.

items.title: 'What's the lowest number you'll perform for?': Rove's awkward MICF gig
items.description: The very first Melbourne International Comedy Festival launched 40 years ago, and while it's kept its scrappy charm, things look pretty different today.

items.title: Married at First Sight expert remembered as 'radiant' after bowel cancer death
items.description: Mel Schilling became one of Australian TV's most recognised relationship experts, but who was she, and what led to her death?

items.title: Travel quiz: Do you have the stamina to complete this trip?
items.description: Which country has the dong as its currency? And where would you dine on tteokbokki?

items.title: 'The day has come': Liverpool great announces he is leaving EPL giant
items.description: Mo Salah announces he is leaving Liverpool after almost a decade of starring for the EPL giants.

items.title: Despite exciting racing F1's major talking point is on pit wall
items.description: Formula 1 has produced drama on and off the track in the early stages of the 2026 season, with focus squarely on the team principal roles of two teams.

items.title: Star Aussie swimmer 'dumbfounded' by $2m prize for doped athletes
items.description: Australian swimmer and 50m freestyle world record holder Cam McEvoy says it is "ludicrous" that doped-up swimmers are being offered as much as $2 million to break a world record, while his legitimate mark earned him nothing.

items.title: Location of Brisbane's new 63,000-seat stadium unveiled
items.description: New artist impressions showing the interior of the 63,000-seat arena have also been released.

items.title: Danish PM's party on track for worst election in over 100 years
items.description: Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen's Social Democrats look set to suffer the party's worst election outcome in more than a century.

items.title: Russia fires nearly 400 drones at Ukraine with signs its spring offensive has begun
items.description: Russia's anticipated annual spring offensive appears to have started, with a major drone assault on civilian areas coinciding with multiple attempts to break through frontline Ukrainian defences.

items.title: 'So lucky': Burke warns failed Perth bomb attack could have killed many
items.description: The home affairs minister says Australia was "so lucky" to avoid mass casualties during the attempted Australia Day bomb attack in Perth and admits the nation was slow to recognise the gravity of the alleged terrorist act.

items.title: How The Kates' fascination with crocodiles shaped their crime comedy show
items.description: Kate McLennan and Kate McCartney (Get Krack!n) set out to make a "funny Broadchurch" with crime comedy Deadloch. Now, with fans around the world, it's back for season two.
